question.worked_solution:
First, we find the smallest and largest $y$-values in the graph.

- The smallest $y$-value is $-1.$ This occurs when $x\to \infty .$ However, note that this point is not included in the graph.

- The largest $y$-value is $3.$ This occurs when $x\to -\infty .$ However, note that this point is not included in the graph.

The function covers all the $y$-values between $-1$ and $3,$ not including $-1$ and $3.$

Therefore, the range is $-1<y<3,$ which can also be written as $-1<f(x)<3.$
